description:
## Target
Wire the existing Layer 3 validation-policy / validator-runtime surfaces into live daemon control flow so they are not test-only helpers.

## Why
Blocked-lane review after `testproject1-hmw.31` and `testproject1-4r5k` still shows a production/runtime gap: validation policy and validator enqueue/persist surfaces exist, but current references are dominated by tests and dead helper wrappers in `main.rs`.

## Candidate Paths
- `crates/daemon/src/main.rs`
- `crates/daemon/src/jobs/runner.rs`
- `crates/daemon/src/validation/executor.rs`
- `crates/daemon/src/validation/policy.rs`
- `crates/daemon/src/ipc/command_router.rs`

## Evidence
- `evaluate_validation_policy(...)` and blind-demotion logic are referenced from tests, but no obvious live caller currently feeds runtime metadata into the policy engine.
- `enqueue_validator_followup(...)`, `enqueue_validation_canary(...)`, and `enqueue_retroactive_validation(...)` exist in `main.rs` as wrappers, but there is no visible production call path reaching them.
- `persist_validation_verdict(...)` is exposed through `JobRunner`, but review of current production surfaces does not show an obvious end-to-end runtime consumer beyond tests.

## Success Criteria
1. The validation policy engine is invoked from live runtime flow with real job/session/source metadata.
2. Validator sub-jobs and verdict persistence are exercised by production code paths rather than helper/test-only plumbing.
3. The resulting runtime integration is covered by explicit tests and passes `cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check && cargo test`.

title: l3-p6-promotion-metadata-followup
description:
## Target
Tighten the L3 promotion-bookkeeping implementation so the new metadata is consumed mechanically and exposed consistently to validator/runtime/test surfaces.

## Why
Blocked-session review of `testproject1-hmw.30` found two concrete gaps after commit `24bc223`:
1. `crates/daemon/src/validation/executor.rs` still parses only the old validator frontmatter contract and emits a flat validator `skill_binding`.
2. `crates/daemon/tests/support/skills.rs` and `crates/daemon/tests/skill_lint.rs` still validate only the pre-L3 metadata contract, so the new promotion/version/calibration fields are not test-visible or mechanically enforced.
3. `crates/daemon/src/main.rs` carries `version_change_affects_behavior`, but the default `worker_behavior_version()` derivation still ignores that flag, and `skill_binding_payload()` sources `source_structure_version` from optional skill frontmatter instead of the source-registry truth.

## Target Paths
- `crates/daemon/src/main.rs`
- `crates/daemon/src/validation/executor.rs`
- `crates/daemon/tests/support/skills.rs`
- `crates/daemon/tests/skill_lint.rs`

## Spec / TDD Anchors
- `L3-FR-3.2.1`
- `L3-FR-3.2.2`
- `L3-FR-2.9.3`
- `L3-T-skill_shadow_compare-004`
- `L3-T-validation_policy-014`
- `L3-T-validation_policy-015`

## Success Criteria
1. Validator/runtime parsing surfaces can ingest the new promotion/version/calibration metadata without silently dropping it.
2. Skill-lint/test helper surfaces make the new metadata visible and enforce the intended contract where appropriate.
3. Cosmetic edits marked non-behavior-affecting can preserve exact-slice readiness mechanically instead of relying on a passive flag with no effect.
4. `source_structure_version` flows from the source-registry truth rather than ad hoc optional skill frontmatter.
5. Rust quality gates pass: `cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`.

- **Strategy**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-strategy.md` — Phase 6 (ordering context only)

## Context

Create two shared UI components with critical security boundaries: `ManifestViewer` (sanitized Markdown renderer) and `ErrorSummaryList` (typed error list). Agent-authored content is UNTRUSTED INPUT.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `typescript`
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `bun run build`
  - `bun run test`

## Files to Create

- `packages/ui/manifest-viewer.tsx` — Sanitized Markdown manifest renderer with section navigation
- `packages/ui/error-summary-list.tsx` — Compact error manifest list with severity/resolution status
- `packages/ui/tests/components.test.tsx` — Shared UI component tests (home for all TS-UI-* tests)

## Spec Requirements (from §1.11, §2.3)

**L2-FR-UI.3 — `ManifestViewer` Renders Sanitized, Navigable Opportunity Manifests**
- AC1: Renders manifest Markdown with section navigation, blocker highlighting, and print-friendly layout.
- AC2: Raw HTML passthrough is disabled and dangerous link schemes are stripped.
- AC3: Section copy and navigation affordances operate on parsed section structure.

**L2-FR-UI.6 — `ErrorSummaryList` Surfaces Sanitized, Typed Error Summaries**
- AC1: Accepts typed `ErrorSummaryItem` rows and resolve/click callbacks.
- AC2: Severity derivation follows the rule set in the spec.
- AC3: Error messages and context are sanitized before rendering.

**L2-FR-SEC.1 — Agent-Authored Content Is Sanitized Before Rendering**
- AC1: `ManifestViewer`, `ErrorSummaryList`, and `SessionViewer` treat agent-authored text as untrusted input.
- AC2: Markdown renderers disable raw HTML and strip `javascript:` and unsafe `file://` links.

**L2-FR-UI.11 — Read-Only Surfaces Omit Mutating Error Actions**
- AC1: `onResolveClick` is optional and may be `null` for read-only consumers.

## Tests to Pass

- **TS-UI-003**: `ManifestViewer` renders navigable sections, preserves copyable section ids, uses sanitized markdown output only
- **TS-UI-006**: `ErrorSummaryList` renders typed rows, honors optional `onResolveClick = null`, and functions without mutable surface

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `ManifestViewer` sanitizes Markdown: no raw HTML, no dangerous links
2. `ErrorSummaryList` accepts typed rows with optional resolve callback
3. Both components are pure presentational with no backend imports
4. Tests TS-UI-003 and TS-UI-006 pass

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-01a
- **Blocks:** l2-07a
- **Phase:** 6 — Shared UI Surfaces

## Component Props (from spec §1.11 — verbatim)

```tsx
interface ManifestViewerProps {
  manifestMarkdown: string
  manifestVersion: string
  basisHash: string
  generatedAt: string
  sections?: string[]           // Parsed section headings for sidebar nav
  highlightBlockers?: boolean   // Visually highlight blocker sections
  onSectionClick?: (sectionId: string) => void
}

interface ErrorSummaryItem {
  errorManifestId: string
  processId: string | null
  pipelineStage: string | null
  errorType: string
  errorMessage: string
  cleanupVerdict?: "clean" | "forced" | "leaked" | null
  severity: "critical" | "warning" | "info"
  createdAt: string
  resolved: boolean
  resolvedAt?: string
}

interface ErrorSummaryListProps {
  errors: ErrorSummaryItem[]
  onErrorClick?: (errorManifestId: string) => void
  onResolveClick?: (errorManifestId: string) => void  // null on web (read-only)
}
```

## Severity Derivation Rules (from spec §1.11 — verbatim)

- **critical**: `AGENT_CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE`, `AGENT_DAEMON_CRASH_DURING_SESSION`, `HOST_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `DAEMON_STARTUP_FAILED`, or any error row whose linked session records `cleanupVerdict = leaked`
- **warning**: all remaining `AGENT_*`, `HOST_SLEEP_INTERRUPTED`, all `SOURCE_*`, `AUTH_STATE_STALE`, `PAGE_SHAPE_DRIFT`, `LOCALE_OR_CURRENCY_DRIFT`, pipeline-quality errors (`NOTICE_PARSE_FAILED`, `GOODS_CLASSIFICATION_LOW_CONFIDENCE`, `SUPPLIER_MATCH_LOW_CONFIDENCE`, `COMMODITY_CODE_LOW_CONFIDENCE`, `REVENUE_BASIS_UNCERTAIN`, `FPO_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE`), and `SQLITE_WRITE_FAILED`
- **info**: reserved for future non-error advisories; L2 `error_manifests` rows do not currently emit informational severities

**Severity ownership:** QueryService or page-level mapper derives `severity` before the shared component renders. `ErrorSummaryList` does not inspect raw error codes.

description:

## Context

Adopt `src-tauri` into the root Cargo workspace and create the native Tauri bootstrap `main.rs`. This converges only once daemon/service and app contracts exist.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `mixed` (Rust + workspace config)
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `cargo check --all-targets`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`

## Files to Modify/Create

- `Cargo.toml` — Root workspace membership update to adopt `apps/desktop/src-tauri`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` — Tauri Rust bootstrap: DB check, daemon handshake, QueryService + DaemonBridge init

## Spec Requirements (from §1.7, §1.9)

**L2-FR-BOOT.6 — Desktop Startup Auto-Launches the Daemon When Possible**
- AC1: Bootstrap performs the startup sequence: DB checks, descriptor read, handshake attempt, detached daemon launch if needed, retry, then mode fallback.
- AC2: The operator is not required to start the daemon manually.

**L2-FR-BOOT.8 — Descriptor Read Precedes Detached Launch**
**L2-FR-BOOT.9 — Auto-Launch Is Single-Flight**

## Tests to Pass

- **CI-L2-001**: `cargo check --all-targets` exits 0 for root workspace including desktop Rust crate
- **CI-L2-002**: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0
- **CI-L2-003**: `cargo fmt --check` exits 0
- **CI-L2-007**: Every `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/*.rs` file starts with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root Cargo workspace includes `apps/desktop/src-tauri`, and every desktop Rust source/test file carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
2. `src-tauri/src/main.rs` executes the startup sequence in spec order: quick-check/schema verification, descriptor read, handshake attempt, one detached daemon launch, bounded retry, then explicit mode fallback.
3. Descriptor read precedes detached launch, and a stale descriptor alone never counts as a healthy daemon.
4. Auto-launch is single-flight: repeated bootstrap transitions or multiple windows do not fan out duplicate daemon launches.
5. Protocol/schema incompatibility becomes an explicit incompatible-mode outcome rather than a generic transport failure.
6. All CI gates CI-L2-001, CI-L2-002, CI-L2-003, and CI-L2-007 pass.

title: l2-08b: QueryService Read-Only Bridge
description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

- **Strategy**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-strategy.md` — Phase 8 (ordering context only)

## Context

Implement the QueryService: read-only SQLite queries returning `QueryEnvelope<T>` with `snapshotSeq` sourced from `commit_clock(id = 1)`. This is the desktop-side snapshot read model for contract list/detail, sessions, errors, and session history, including canonical-process resolution through `process_aliases` and explicit `complete|partial|missing` replay availability for archived session chunks.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `rust`
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `cargo test --test query_service`
  - `cargo check --all-targets`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`

## Files to Create

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/query_service.rs` — Read-only SQLite queries returning `QueryEnvelope<T>`
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/query_service.rs` — QueryService contract tests

## Spec Requirements (from §1.4)

**L2-FR-QS.1 — QueryService Is Read-Only, Page-Scoped, and Non-Streaming**
**L2-FR-QS.2 — Snapshot Envelopes and the Commit Fence Are Normative**
**L2-FR-QS.3 — The User-Visible Snapshot Clock Is `commit_seq`**
**L2-FR-QS.4 — `list_processes()` Returns a Stable Keyset Page**
**L2-FR-QS.5 — `get_process_detail()` Returns a Complete Detail Read Model**
**L2-FR-QS.6 — `list_sessions()` Returns Canonical Session Metadata**
**L2-FR-QS.7 — `list_errors()` Returns the Operator Error Queue**
**L2-FR-QS.8 — QueryService Read Failures Are Explicit and Non-Mutating**
**L2-FR-QS.9 — Process and Detail Read Models Are Fully Typed**
**L2-FR-QS.10 — Session and Error Read Models Are Fully Typed**
**L2-FR-QS.11 — Query Filters Are Explicit and Validated**
**L2-FR-QS.12 — Session History Replay Uses an On-Demand Read Contract**
**L2-FR-QS.13 — QueryService Errors Are Typed**

## Ground-Truth Storage Anchors

Use the current repository truth rather than inventing tables or clocks:
- `crates/daemon/src/db/sqlite.rs` seeds `commit_clock (id = 1)` and the `sources` / `source_runtime_state` rows.
- `migrations/0001_sqlite_state_initial.sql` defines `procurement_processes`, `contract_notices`, `notice_lots`, `product_candidates`, `supplier_quotes`, and related core read-model tables. QueryService route resolution must also honor `process_aliases`; if the checked-in schema snapshot is still missing that table, close the schema gap in the same bead before deep-link routing is considered complete.
- `crates/daemon/src/db/sqlite.rs` runtime schema extension owns `agent_session_logs` column additions used by session reads.
- Session-history replay reads archived chunk metadata/payloads and must surface `availability = complete | partial | missing` rather than inventing continuity from the hot live buffer.
- The decision overlay table consumed later by QueryService is `pending_operator_intents` from `migrations/0004_l2_pending_operator_intents.sql`.

## Tests to Pass

- **RS-QS-001** through **RS-QS-012**

## Acceptance Criteria

1. QueryService uses `PRAGMA query_only = ON` and performs no writes.
2. `snapshotSeq` comes from `commit_clock.commit_seq`, never from `PRAGMA data_version`.
3. `list_processes`, `get_process_detail`, `list_sessions`, `list_errors`, and `get_session_history` are all typed page-scoped read contracts, with `get_session_history` preserving `complete | partial | missing` availability.
4. `get_process_detail()` resolves canonical process detail through `process_aliases` before returning not-found so bookmarked/merged process ids stay navigable.
5. Read failures stay typed and non-mutating.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-08a
- **Blocks:** l2-09a, l2-09b, l2-10b, l2-10c, l2-11a
- **Phase:** 8 — Desktop Rust Bridge And Native Bootstrap

title: l2-08c: DaemonBridge RPC Proxy
description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

This bead is a quick-reference derived from:
- **Spec**: `docs/strategy/layers/layer-2-single-operator-desktop.md` — §1.5 (PRIMARY — read this first)
- **TDD**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-tdd.md` — RS-DBR-001 through RS-DBR-007 (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-strategy.md` — Phase 8 (ordering context only)

## Context

Implement the DaemonBridge: thin RPC proxy forwarding 11 daemon methods over UDS/named pipe. It owns handshake adaptation, typed request/response routing, and retry-aware bridge errors, but it does not become authoritative for writes.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `rust`
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `cargo test --test daemon_bridge`
  - `cargo check --all-targets`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`

## Files to Create

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/daemon_bridge.rs` — Desktop-side RPC proxy to daemon over UDS/named pipe
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/daemon_bridge.rs` — Bridge contract tests

## Spec Requirements (from §1.5)

**L2-FR-DB.1 — DaemonBridge Is a Thin RPC Proxy**
**L2-FR-DB.14 — Bridge Failure Paths Are Explicit and Operator-Visible**
**L2-FR-DB.15 — Layer 2 Extends the Handshake-Only IPC Envelope**
**L2-FR-DB.16 — Every Command Has a Typed Input Contract**
**L2-FR-DB.17 — Command Dispatch Is Mechanically Mapped to Daemon Handlers**
**L2-FR-DB.18 — Bridge Errors Are Typed and Retry-Aware**
**L2-FR-DB.19 — Bridge Request Kinds Form a Closed Wire Contract**
**L2-FR-DB.20 — Welcome Frames Carry the Full Control-Plane Snapshot**
**L2-FR-DB.21 — `get_daemon_info()` Completes the Daemon Diagnostics Surface**

## Ground-Truth Wire Anchors

Align to the current daemon handshake truth in `crates/daemon/src/ipc/handshake.rs`:
- `ClientMessage::Hello { desktop_version, supported_protocol_range, expected_schema_epoch, last_seen_instance_id }`
- `ServerMessage::Welcome { selected_protocol_version, daemon_version, instance_id, schema_epoch, commit_seq, health_state, mutations_allowed, active_sessions, reconnect_outcome, stream_resume_permitted }`
- raw pre-router mutation traffic still rejects as `mutations_unavailable`

The bridge must forward these 11 daemon methods exactly: `get_daemon_info`, `trigger_ingestion`, `trigger_enrichment`, `capture_decision`, `resolve_error`, `stop_session`, `send_session_input`, `resize_session`, `retry_job`, `restart_daemon`, `rerun_from_error`.

## Tests to Pass

- **RS-DBR-001** through **RS-DBR-007**

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The bridge remains a thin RPC proxy with no authoritative writes.
2. All 11 daemon methods preserve typed params/results and request-kind rules.
3. Transport failures remain distinct from daemon refusals, with stable retryability hints.
4. Welcome-handshake state matches the current daemon wire contract.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-08a
- **Blocks:** l2-09a, l2-09b, l2-10a
- **Phase:** 8 — Desktop Rust Bridge And Native Bootstrap

title: l2-09a: Contract List And Detail Pages
description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

## Context

Create the first read-only operator browse surfaces: `ContractList.tsx` (keyset-paginated process list) and `ContractDetail.tsx` (full opportunity detail with manifest, coverage, and errors). This bead also owns the page-level accessibility and deep-link stability contract: live updates must not steal focus, and `/process/:processId` must stay navigable through canonical-id / alias resolution rather than brittle row positions.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `typescript`
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `bunx playwright test e2e/contracts.spec.ts`

## Files to Create

- `apps/desktop/src/pages/ContractList.tsx` — Keyset-paginated process list
- `apps/desktop/src/pages/ContractDetail.tsx` — Full opportunity detail view
- `apps/desktop/e2e/contracts.spec.ts` — List/detail browsing E2E tests

## Spec Requirements (from §1.9)

**L2-FR-PAGE.1 — Contract List Surfaces the Daily Opportunity Queue**
- AC1: List page renders `list_processes()` results with keyset pagination, pipeline badges, coverage summaries, and decision status.
- AC2: Empty-result states render explicitly with filter-aware empty messaging.
- AC3: Live updates do not cause row jumping or focus loss.

**L2-FR-PAGE.2 — Contract Detail Surfaces the Full Review Packet**
- AC1: Detail page renders notices, lots, candidates, quotes, margin outputs, manifest, and errors.
- AC2: Zero-lot processes render explicit empty states.
- AC3: Decision status and staleness are visible on the detail surface.

**L2-FR-PAGE.8, L2-FR-PAGE.9** — Query and navigation contracts.
**L2-FR-PAG.1, L2-FR-PAG.2** — Keyset pagination and empty/terminal page semantics.
**L2-FR-COV.1, L2-FR-COV.3** — Coverage metrics presentation and threshold labels.
**L2-FR-A11Y.2 (page-owned ACs)** — keyset updates keep focus stable and deep-linked process identities remain resolvable through canonical / alias routing.

## Tests to Pass

- **PW-CON-001**: List page renders 25 rows from one envelope; first row shows title, buyer, deadline, badges, decision summary
- **PW-CON-002**: Empty query renders explicit empty-state copy; `hasMore = false`
- **PW-CON-003**: Next-page uses cursor not offset; no duplicate `processId`; last page `nextCursor = null`
- **PW-CON-004**: Live insert does not reorder visible rows; focus stays on selected row
- **PW-CON-005**: Filter normalization; invalid filter values rejected before partial rendering
- **PW-CON-006**: Expired non-DPS absent; expired DPS visible
- **PW-CON-007**: Detail page renders full review packet in integer-pence/bps-derived formats
- **PW-CON-008**: Zero-lot process shows explicit empty-state copy
- **PW-CON-009**: Empty candidates/quotes render explicit placeholders; coverage shows zero values
- **PW-CON-010**: Both lot-count and value-weighted gate results visible; failed value-weighted warning shown

## Acceptance Criteria

1. ContractList uses keyset pagination, not offset, and live inserts do not reorder already-visible rows or steal focus.
2. ContractDetail renders the full review packet from one detail read model.
3. `/process/:processId` remains deep-link stable: canonical or aliased process ids resolve to the same detail surface via QueryService alias resolution rather than brittle row-position routing.
4. Empty states are explicit, not errors.
5. All tests PW-CON-001 through PW-CON-010 pass.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-05a, l2-05b, l2-07b, l2-08b, l2-08c
- **Blocks:** l2-11a
- **Phase:** 9 — Read-Only Operator Pages

## Playwright Test Setup (from spec §4.1)

Before running Playwright tests in this bead:
1. Start daemon (background): `cargo run -p daemon -- serve`
2. Start Vite dev server: `bun run dev` → `localhost:5173` with dev bridge plugin active
3. Run tests: `bunx playwright test` → Chromium navigates to `localhost:5173`

The dev bridge (spec §1.8) provides full daemon access in a plain browser. All UI E2E tests run against the same app contract as the Tauri webview.

## Page Query Types (from spec §1.9 — verbatim)

```typescript
type ContractListPageQuery = {
  after?: string
  limit?: 25 | 50
  search?: string
  sourceId?: string
  pipelineState?: ProcessListFilters["pipelineStates"][number]
  decision?: ProcessListFilters["decisionDispositions"][number]
  staleOnly?: "true" | "false"
}

type SessionViewerRoute = {
  sessionId: string
  initialMode?: "live" | "history"
}
```

**Routes consumed by these pages:**
- `ContractList.tsx` → `/` (list with `ContractListPageQuery`)

title: l2-10a: Session Registry And Buffer Stores
description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

This bead is a quick-reference derived from:
- **Spec**: `docs/strategy/layers/layer-2-single-operator-desktop.md` — §1.10 (PRIMARY — read this first)
- **TDD**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-tdd.md` — TS-REG-001 through TS-REG-005, TS-BUF-001 through TS-BUF-004 (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-strategy.md` — Phase 10 (ordering context only)

## Context

Create the purpose-built external stores for live session state: `SessionRegistry` (metadata, `lastSeq`, gap state, archive fence) and `SessionBuffer` (PTY bytes or contract-mode frames with explicit gap markers). NOT TanStack Query.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `typescript`
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `bun run test`

## Files to Create

- `apps/desktop/src/stores/session-registry.ts` — External store for session metadata and replay anchors
- `apps/desktop/src/stores/session-registry.test.ts` — Session registry tests
- `apps/desktop/src/stores/session-buffer.ts` — Per-session buffer (PTY bytes or text frames)
- `apps/desktop/src/stores/session-buffer.test.ts` — Session buffer tests

## Spec Requirements (from §1.10)

**L2-FR-STATE.1 — Snapshot, Streaming, and Control-Plane State Stay Separated**
**L2-FR-STATE.2 — Session Output Never Lives as Raw React Component State**
- AC1: PTY buffers store bytes rather than pre-expanded React-friendly line arrays.
- AC2: Contract-mode history stores structured text/event frames with explicit gap markers.

**L2-FR-STATE.5 — Replay State Is First-Class in the Registry**
**L2-FR-STATE.7 — Session Buffer Has an Explicit Frame API**
**L2-FR-STATE.8 — `lastSeq` Persistence Is Restart-Aware**

## Key Types (from spec §1.10 — verbatim)

```typescript
type SessionRegistryApi = {
  getSnapshot(): SessionRegistryState
  subscribe(onStoreChange: () => void): () => void
  resetForDaemon(instanceId: string): void
  applySessionMeta(session: SessionListItem): void
  applyStreamFrame(sessionId: string, frame: SessionFrame): void
  markReplayResolved(sessionId: string, fromSeq: number, toSeq: number): void
}
```

## Tests to Pass

- **TS-REG-001**: Registry stores sessions by `daemonInstanceId + sessionId`; metadata upserts do not clobber unrelated sessions
- **TS-REG-002**: Stream frames advance `lastSeq` monotonically; out-of-order rejected/buffered
- **TS-REG-003**: Gap state records exact `fromSeq..toSeq`; replay resolution clears matching range only
- **TS-REG-004**: `archiveSeq` tracked; prevents historical handoff until snapshot fence satisfied
- **TS-REG-005**: Same-daemon reopen preserves `lastSeq`; daemon instance change clears anchors
- **TS-BUF-001**: PTY buffer stores bytes not lines; tail extraction derived without mutating authoritative storage
- **TS-BUF-002**: Contract buffer stores text/event frames with gap markers; frame kind preserved through replay
- **TS-BUF-003**: Replay merge inserts by original `seq` without duplicating present frames
- **TS-BUF-004**: Bounded pruning retains tail context and visible unresolved-gap markers

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `SessionRegistry` uses `useSyncExternalStore` pattern
2. PTY buffers store bytes, not lines
3. Gap state is first-class with explicit `fromSeq..toSeq`
4. `lastSeq` persistence is restart-aware
5. All tests TS-REG-001-005 and TS-BUF-001-004 pass

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-04c, l2-07b, l2-08c
- **Blocks:** l2-10b
- **Phase:** 10 — Streaming And Session UX Lane

title: l2-11a: Decision Migration And Handler
description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

This bead is a quick-reference derived from:
- **Spec**: `docs/strategy/layers/layer-2-single-operator-desktop.md` — §3.2, §3.3 (PRIMARY — read this first)
- **TDD**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-tdd.md` — PW-DEC-001 through PW-DEC-008, PW-FEN-001 through PW-FEN-007 (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-strategy.md` — Phase 11 (ordering context only)

## Context

Create the `pending_operator_intents` SQLite migration and the `capture_decision` daemon handler. This is the first operator mutation surface: local intent queue for approve/reject/watch decisions with reviewed-basis metadata and staleness detection.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `mixed` (Rust handler + SQL migration + TypeScript page wiring)
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `bunx playwright test e2e/decisions.spec.ts e2e/commit-fence.spec.ts`
  - `cargo test -p daemon --test agent_supplier_enrichment`

## Files to Create

- `migrations/0004_l2_pending_operator_intents.sql` — Decision overlay table from L0 §2.5.8 DDL
- `crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/decisions.rs` — `capture_decision` handler
- `apps/desktop/e2e/decisions.spec.ts` — Decision capture E2E tests
- `apps/desktop/e2e/commit-fence.spec.ts` — Commit-fence mutation visibility tests
- `crates/daemon/tests/agent_supplier_enrichment.rs` — Enrichment agent E2E tests

## Spec Requirements (from §3.2)

**L2-FR-DEC.1 — Each Local Decision Captures the Reviewed Basis**
- AC1: Every decision intent records: `process_id`, `desired_disposition`, `reviewed_basis_hash`, `reviewed_manifest_hash`, `reviewed_at_stage_run_id`, `reviewed_at`, `base_remote_revision`, `idempotency_key`, `status`, `superseded_by_intent_id`, `queued_at`.
- AC2: `reviewedBasisHash` copied from daemon-authored pipeline assessment, NOT recomputed in UI.

**L2-FR-DEC.2 — Latest-Per-Process Coalescing Is Explicit**
- AC1: Only the latest queued intent per process is the current local decision.
- AC2: Newer decision supersedes via `superseded_by_intent_id`.

**L2-FR-DEC.3 — Decision Staleness Is Hash-Based and Operator-Visible**
- AC1: Desktop compares `reviewedBasisHash` against `pipeline_assessments.decisionBasisHash`; mismatch = stale.

**L2-FR-DEC.4 — `pending_operator_intents` Reuses the Layer 0 DDL Exactly**
**L2-FR-DB.6 — `capture_decision()` Persists the Operator Intent**

## Tests to Pass

- **PW-DEC-001**: Approve returns committed ack; `pending_operator_intents` row stores all required fields
- **PW-DEC-002**: Watch action persists and shows after commit fence clears
- **PW-DEC-003**: Approve then reject creates two rows; first superseded; UI shows reject
- **PW-DEC-004**: Re-affirming same disposition writes new intent with new key
- **PW-DEC-005**: Decision on hash A becomes stale after rerun produces hash B
- **PW-DEC-006**: Rerun with same hash does NOT mark stale
- **PW-DEC-007**: Lost ack retry with same idempotency key returns same ack; one row
- **PW-DEC-008**: Pre-fence shows old; post-fence shows new; no ghost state
- **PW-FEN-001**: `trigger_ingestion()` fence semantics
- **PW-FEN-002**: `trigger_enrichment()` fence semantics
- **PW-FEN-003**: Capture-decision fence preserves old until clears
- **PW-FEN-004**: Resolve error fence
- **PW-FEN-005**: Retry job fence
- **PW-FEN-006**: Rollback advances no fence; archive handoff obeys archiveSeq
- **PW-FEN-007**: Concurrent mutations ordered `visibleAfterSeq` values
- **AG-ENR-001 through AG-ENR-004**: Enrichment happy path, confidence, scoped rerun, partial data

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `pending_operator_intents` table matches L0 §2.5.8 DDL exactly
2. `capture_decision` handler writes reviewed-basis metadata
3. Latest-per-process coalescing via `superseded_by_intent_id`
4. Decision staleness detected via `decisionBasisHash` comparison
5. All commit-fence tests verify pre/post visibility semantics
6. All tests pass: PW-DEC-001-008, PW-FEN-001-007, AG-ENR-001-004

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-05b, l2-08b, l2-09a, l2-09b
- **Blocks:** l2-11b
- **Phase:** 11 — Decisions, Coverage, Staleness, And Operator Validation Package

## Playwright Test Setup (from spec §4.1)

Before running Playwright tests in this bead:
1. Start daemon (background): `cargo run -p daemon -- serve`
2. Start Vite dev server: `bun run dev` → `localhost:5173` with dev bridge plugin active
3. Run tests: `bunx playwright test` → Chromium navigates to `localhost:5173`

The dev bridge (spec §1.8) provides full daemon access in a plain browser. All UI E2E tests run against the same app contract as the Tauri webview.

## Key Types (from spec §1.5, §3.2 — verbatim)

```typescript
type CaptureDecisionParams = {
  processId: string
  disposition: "approve" | "reject" | "watch"
  reviewedBasisHash: string
  reviewedManifestHash: string
  reviewedAtStageRunId: string
}
```

## `pending_operator_intents` DDL Contract (from spec §3.2, L0 §2.5.8)

The migration must create a table with these columns exactly:

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` | UUID |
| `process_id` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | Target process |
| `desired_disposition` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | approve / reject / watch |
| `reviewed_basis_hash` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | SHA-256 of pipeline data at decision time |
| `reviewed_manifest_hash` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | SHA-256 of manifest reviewed |
| `reviewed_at_stage_run_id` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | Current stage_run_id at decision time |
| `reviewed_at` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | Timestamp of operator review |
| `base_remote_revision` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Always 0 in L2 (no remote) |
| `idempotency_key` | `TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` | UUID for CAS dedup (Layer 4) |
| `status` | `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT "queued"` | Always "queued" in L2 |
| `superseded_by_intent_id` | `TEXT` | Links to newer intent for same process |
| `queued_at` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | Local enqueue timestamp |
| `decision_note` | `TEXT` | Optional operator note |
| `last_attempt_at` | `TEXT` | NULL in L2 |
| `last_error` | `TEXT` | NULL in L2 |

**Coalescing rule:** Only the latest intent per `process_id` matters. Newer decisions set `superseded_by_intent_id` on the older row.

title: l2-12a: Contracts Finder Skill Package
description:

## Context

Create the Contracts Finder ingestion skill package, mirroring the FTS skill structure exactly. This is an independent daemon/skill lane — NO dependencies on desktop beads. Only depends on the daemon command lane (Phase 4).

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `mixed` (skill playbook + Rust daemon test)
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `cargo test -p daemon --test agent_contracts_finder_ingestion`

## Files to Create

- `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/SKILL.md` — CF ingestion skill playbook
- `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/checkpoint.schema.json` — Checkpoint schema
- `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/result.schema.json` — Result schema
- `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/canary.inputs.jsonl` — Canary test inputs
- `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/golden.assertions.yaml` — Golden assertions
- `crates/daemon/tests/agent_contracts_finder_ingestion.rs` — CF agent E2E tests

## Spec Requirements (from §1.13)

**L2-FR-CF.1 — Contracts Finder Ingestion Is a First-Class Layer 2 Source Skill**
- AC1: Layer 2 adds a skill at `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/`.
- AC2: The skill declares a `pty_interactive` interaction profile.
- AC3: Cursor handling is rate-limit-aware and stable for repeated daily ingestion.

**L2-FR-CF.2 — Contracts Finder Skill Packaging Matches the FTS Standard**
- AC1: Same structural sections as FTS: use/do-not-use, inputs, outputs, failure codes, resume strategy, canary, run-manifest instructions.
- AC2: Checkpoint-safe continuation semantics.
- AC3: Cursor overlap/backtrack behavior documented explicitly.

**L2-FR-CF.3 — Contracts Finder Canary and Manifest Rules Are Mandatory**
- AC1: Lightweight canary before full retrieval; fail fast on drift.
- AC2: Same run-manifest frontmatter and narrative sections as FTS.
- AC3: Source drift and rate-limit issues surface as explicit failure codes.

## Tests to Pass

- **AG-CF-001**: Skill directory contains SKILL.md, checkpoint.schema.json, result.schema.json, canary.inputs.jsonl, golden.assertions.yaml
- **AG-CF-002**: Canary validates recent response shape, locale, currency, rate-limit expectations
- **AG-CF-003**: Incremental run emits notices + checkpoint; `continuation_required` when time budget expires
- **AG-CF-004**: Cursor backtrack prevents skipped notices; no duplicate durable notice ids
- **AG-CF-005**: Run manifest includes required YAML frontmatter and narrative sections
- **AG-CF-006**: Source drift, locale drift, soft block, CAPTCHA, stall emit explicit failure codes

## Acceptance Criteria

1. CF skill mirrors FTS five-file skeleton exactly
2. Canary validates before full retrieval
3. Incremental cursor with backtrack window
4. Run manifest matches FTS standard
5. All tests AG-CF-001 through AG-CF-006 pass

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** l2-04b (daemon command lane only — independent of desktop beads)
- **Blocks:** l2-12b
- **Phase:** 12 — Contracts Finder Skill Lane, Hardening, And Milestone Gate

## Contracts Finder API Parameters (from spec §1.13 — verbatim)

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Path** | `skills/procurement-ingestion/contracts-finder/` |
| **Interaction profile** | `pty_interactive` |
| **API** | OCDS/Search API: `publishedFrom`, `publishedTo`, `stages`, `limit`, `cursor`. Rate limiting documented. |
| **Cursor strategy** | Date-based filtering + cursor; rate-limit-aware polling |

**Inputs:** `source_cursors` watermark plus optional `publishedFrom`, `publishedTo`, `stages`, `cursor`, and `limit` job parameters.
**Outputs:** Structured notice batch, checkpoint-friendly partial progress, and `continuation_required` when safe remaining work exceeds the time budget.

**Failure codes:** `SOURCE_CHANGED`, `AGENT_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH`, `SOURCE_SOFT_BLOCKED`, `SOURCE_CAPTCHA_BLOCKED`, `PAGE_SHAPE_DRIFT`, `LOCALE_OR_CURRENCY_DRIFT`, `AGENT_STALLED`.

**Resume strategy:** Cursor backtrack window with small overlap so incremental runs never skip notices if Contracts Finder mutates during retrieval.

## FTS Skill Reference Structure

The CF skill MUST mirror the five-file skeleton in `skills/procurement-ingestion/fts/`:
1. `SKILL.md` — Use/do-not-use guidance, inputs, outputs, failure codes, resume strategy, canary, run-manifest instructions
2. `checkpoint.schema.json` — Checkpoint state schema
3. `result.schema.json` — Result contract schema
4. `canary.inputs.jsonl` — Lightweight smoke test inputs
5. `golden.assertions.yaml` — Expected assertion results

Read `skills/procurement-ingestion/fts/SKILL.md` as the structural template before implementing.

description:
## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

This bead is a quick-reference derived from:

- **Strategy**: `docs/pipeline/l2-desktop-mvp/artifacts/l2-desktop-mvp-strategy.md` — Phase 12 (ordering context only)

## Context

Close Phase 12 on the native side: Tauri lifecycle parity, five-mode bootstrap parity, restart-action closure on `DaemonStatus`, desktop-only logs/artifacts affordances, production-build exclusion of the dev bridge, and the final cumulative milestone gate. This bead consumes the Contracts Finder lane from `l2-12a`, the browser hardening lane from `l2-12b`, and the weekly operator checklist from `l2-11b`.

## Language & Quality Gates

- **Language:** `mixed` (Tauri/native verification + cumulative repo gates)
- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `cargo check --all-targets`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `bun run build`
  - `bun run lint`
  - `bun run test`
  - `bunx playwright test --list`
  - `bunx playwright test e2e/tauri-integration.spec.ts e2e/daemon-status.spec.ts`
  - `cargo test -p daemon --test agent_contracts_finder_ingestion`

## Files to Create/Modify

- `apps/desktop/e2e/tauri-integration.spec.ts` — Native Tauri lifecycle and parity coverage
- `apps/desktop/e2e/daemon-status.spec.ts` — Extend daemon-status coverage with restart CTA behavior
- `apps/desktop/src/pages/DaemonStatus.tsx` — Restart CTA gating, descriptor/live diagnostics convergence, and desktop-only open-logs/open-artifacts affordances
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` — Native startup, reconnect, close-vs-quit, and daemon lifecycle behavior
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/transport.ts` — Ensure shipped desktop build resolves native transport without the dev bridge
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` — Final native build/path configuration if parity work requires it

## Spec Requirements

**L2-FR-DB.2 — Handshake Negotiates Compatibility and Restart Semantics**
**L2-FR-DB.12 — `restart_daemon()` Acknowledges Before Disconnection**
**L2-FR-BOOT.3 — Bootstrap Derives One of Five Operator Modes**
**L2-FR-BOOT.4 — Mid-Session Daemon Failure Has a Defined Recovery Path**
**L2-FR-BOOT.5 — Window Close and Daemon Stop Are Separate Operator Actions**
**L2-FR-BOOT.6 — Desktop Startup Auto-Launches the Daemon When Possible**
**L2-FR-BOOT.7 — `ControlPlaneState` Is the Canonical Runtime Health Model**
**L2-FR-BOOT.8 — Descriptor Read Precedes Detached Launch**
**L2-FR-BOOT.9 — Auto-Launch Is Single-Flight**
**L2-FR-BOOT.10 — Browse-Only Mode Has a Narrow, Explicit Capability Set**
**L2-FR-BOOT.11 — Runtime-Mode Derivation Is Total and Non-Overlapping**
**L2-FR-PAGE.13 — `DaemonStatus.tsx` Has an Explicit Diagnostic Action Contract**
**L2-FR-DEV.4 — The Dev Bridge Is Local-Only and Never Shipped**
**L2-FR-SEC.2 — Desktop Capability Exposure Is Least-Privilege**

## Tests to Pass

- **PW-DGN-003**
- **TAU-INT-001** through **TAU-INT-012**
- **CI-L2-006**
- Cumulative milestone gate across the full Layer 2 command set, package set, browser specs, and Contracts Finder skill lane

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Native startup and reconnect behavior honor the documented five-mode matrix: `full control`, `control limited`, `browse-only`, `incompatible`, and `recovery required`.
2. Mid-session daemon failure shows reconnect state, attempts one automatic restart, performs fresh handshake/`instanceId` comparison, never resumes PTY across daemon restart, and falls back to browse-only if restart fails.
3. `DaemonStatus` exposes restart only in allowed modes, returns the restart ack before disconnect, and exposes desktop-only open-logs/open-artifacts diagnostics without leaking those affordances into shared UI packages.
4. Native shell behavior distinguishes `Quit UI` from `Stop background daemon and quit`.
5. Production desktop builds exclude the dev bridge / loopback HTTP control path while still using native invoke/channel successfully.
6. The full cumulative Layer 2 milestone gate passes, including `agent_contracts_finder_ingestion` and the browser-spec discovery gate.
7. The weekly operator checklist from `docs/testing/l2-operator-weekly-validation.md` is ready to run.

## Dependencies

- **Blocks:** none (terminal Layer 2 milestone bead)

title: L2 audit: expose the full Tauri query/mutation surface and stop desktop-local authority leaks
description:
Spec/TDD: L2-FR-QS.4-.13, L2-FR-DB.1,.4-.13,.21, L2-FR-PAGE.5-.6,.9-.13, TAU-INT-011, RS-QS-001..012, RS-DBR-001..010.

Confirmed gaps:
- apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs invoke_handler only registers list_errors/get_daemon_info/restart_daemon/capture_decision/resolve_error/rerun_from_error; native Tauri is missing list_processes, get_process_detail, list_sessions, get_session_history, trigger_ingestion, trigger_enrichment, stop_session, send_session_input, resize_session, and retry_job.
- capture_decision, resolve_error, and rerun_from_error mutate SQLite directly inside the desktop shell instead of proxying through daemon authority.
- get_daemon_info in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs returns a desktop-only payload shape that does not match the daemon bridge contract consumed by apps/desktop/src/pages/DaemonStatus.tsx.

Scope:
- Expose the full QueryService read surface and full bridge-backed mutation surface as Tauri commands.
- Remove desktop-authoritative mutation writes from the shell.
- Return the contract-compatible diagnostics payload required by DaemonStatus.tsx.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: In apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs register native Tauri commands for list_processes, get_process_detail, list_sessions, get_session_history, trigger_ingestion, trigger_enrichment, stop_session, send_session_input, resize_session, and retry_job in the same invoke_handler that already exposes list_errors/get_daemon_info/restart_daemon.
AC2: Remove desktop-authoritative SQLite mutation flows for capture_decision, resolve_error, and rerun_from_error from the Tauri shell path; those commands must call DaemonBridge and must not commit local writes directly from apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs.
AC3: Make get_daemon_info return the bridge-compatible diagnostics payload used by apps/desktop/src/pages/DaemonStatus.tsx: instanceId, daemonVersion, protocolVersion, schemaEpoch, socketPath, descriptorPath, stateRoot, stateDbPath, artifactRoot, walBytes, startedAt, and startupRecovery.
AC4: Native Tauri execution must be able to satisfy the same app-level command names used by App.tsx, Sessions.tsx, SessionViewer.tsx, Errors.tsx, and DaemonStatus.tsx without fixture-only fallbacks.

title: L2 audit: finish daemon IPC command router, typed refusals, and full-control handshake
description:
Spec/TDD: L2-FR-DB.1-.21, L2-FR-BOOT.3,.6,.11, PW-BRD-001..006, TAU-INT-003..011, RS-DBR-001..010.

Confirmed gaps:
- crates/daemon/src/ipc/command_router.rs dispatches get_daemon_info, restart_daemon, trigger_ingestion, trigger_enrichment, retry_job, stop_session, send_session_input, and resize_session only; capture_decision, resolve_error, and rerun_from_error are missing.
- crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers only contains control.rs/jobs.rs/sessions.rs; decisions.rs and errors.rs handler domains from the spec do not exist.
- crates/daemon/src/main.rs build_handshake_context() hard-codes mutations_allowed: false, so a live desktop handshake cannot reach full-control mode.
- Router failures for job/control commands collapse to busy(error.to_string()), losing the typed refusal/error semantics required by the bridge contract.
- restart_daemon() currently returns an ack without owning a restart lifecycle beyond disconnect-after-response.

Scope:
- Add decision/error handler domains and wire them through the closed command-method set.
- Fix handshake mutation allowance/control-mode signaling.
- Return typed bridge errors/not_found/conflict/not_interactive semantics instead of generic busy wrappers.
- Implement real restart-intent handling.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: Add daemon-side handler domains for decisions and errors, with concrete functions for capture_decision, resolve_error, and rerun_from_error under crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/decisions.rs and crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/errors.rs, and wire them through crates/daemon/src/ipc/command_router.rs.
AC2: Make the command router dispatch the full closed L2 method set: get_daemon_info, trigger_ingestion, trigger_enrichment, capture_decision, resolve_error, stop_session, send_session_input, resize_session, retry_job, restart_daemon, rerun_from_error.
AC3: Replace generic busy(error.to_string()) mapping where the spec requires typed refusal semantics; invalid params, not_found, conflict, already_terminal, not_interactive, busy, and artifact_unavailable must survive to the bridge layer with retryable set appropriately.
AC4: In crates/daemon/src/main.rs derive mutations_allowed from the live runtime capability so a healthy daemon can handshake into full-control mode instead of always advertising read-only/limited control.
AC5: restart_daemon must acknowledge before disconnect and must own a real restart intent path rather than returning a synthetic ack with no restart behavior behind it.
notes:
Primary files: crates/daemon/src/ipc/command_router.rs, crates/daemon/src/ipc/handshake.rs, crates/daemon/src/main.rs, crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/control.rs, crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/jobs.rs, new crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/decisions.rs, new crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/errors.rs.
Primary TDD IDs: PW-BRD-001..006, TAU-INT-003..011, RS-DBR-001..010, ipc_handshake it_ipc_003/006/007/012.
close_reason: Fixed: daemon IPC router now dispatches decision/error commands, advertises live full-control mode, and restart flows through a relaunch intent

title: L2 audit: implement end-to-end session and control-plane streaming with real subscribe/replay semantics
description:
Spec/TDD: L2-FR-CH.1-.15, L2-FR-STATE.1-.8, L2-FR-BOOT.4, L2-FR-PAGE.3-.4,.11, PW-SES-003..012, TAU-INT-009..010, AG-HLT-002..005.

Confirmed gaps:
- crates/daemon/src/ipc/handshake.rs rejects subscribe/unsubscribe with busy("stream subscriptions remain unavailable until the session router is active").
- apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-daemon.ts never calls transport subscribe(); session state is snapshot-only.
- apps/desktop/src/pages/SessionViewer.tsx seeds seedDevSessionFrames() instead of consuming live daemon traffic.
- crates/daemon/src/ipc/handlers/sessions.rs still rejects send_session_input() and resize_session() with "live PTY attachment is not available through the command surface yet".
- apps/desktop/src/hooks/use-control-plane.ts has no applyHealthEvent/heartbeat path, so mid-session daemon failure and automatic restart handling are absent.
- apps/desktop/src/stores/session-registry.ts persists lastSeq only in a module-scoped Map, not across desktop close/reopen.

Scope:
- Daemon health/session topic families, metadata-only + full-stream subscriptions, gap signaling, replay requests, PTY input/resize end-to-end, control-plane heartbeat updates, and durable lastSeq persistence keyed by daemonInstanceId + sessionId.
acceptance_criteria:

title: L2 audit: harden QueryService to match the page-scoped SQL and replay contract
description:
Spec/TDD: L2-FR-QS.1-.13, L2-FR-PAG.1-.2, L2-FR-CH.10-.11, PW-CON-001..006, PW-SES-012, RS-QS-001..012.

Confirmed gaps:
- apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/query_service.rs loads full process/session/error sets into memory and applies filters/cursors after the fact instead of page-limited SQL reads.
- QueryService::open() derives runtime_dir from db_path.parent()/runtime, which is wrong for the actual desktop layout where state/ and runtime/ are siblings.
- PTY history replay materializes one Pty frame per chunk at entry.first_seq rather than replaying the original frame sequence range; the history union also omits lifecycle/event/gap frames required for deterministic merge semantics.
- list_processes() does not implement the queue-side expiry/DPS filtering promised by the TDD.

Scope:
- Push filters/cursors into SQL, fix runtime-path plumbing, emit history payloads that preserve original seq coverage and frame kinds, and enforce queue semantics directly in QueryService.
acceptance_criteria:
AC1: Push process/session/error filtering and keyset pagination into SQL so list_processes, list_sessions, and list_errors materialize at most limit + 1 rows before page construction instead of loading whole result sets and filtering in memory.
AC2: Fix QueryService runtime path handling so session metadata/artifact lookup resolves the actual sibling runtime directory for the desktop layout instead of db_path.parent()/runtime when the DB lives under state/state.db.
AC3: Make get_session_history preserve original replay sequence semantics: returned frames must keep the original per-frame seq values across the requested range and must not collapse a whole archived PTY chunk into one frame at first_seq.
AC4: Extend history replay to cover the frame kinds required for deterministic merge and unresolved-gap UX, including explicit partial/missing availability when the artifact range cannot be fully reconstructed.
AC5: Enforce queue-side notice visibility rules inside list_processes, including the expired non-DPS filter and the DPS/dynamic-market exception required by the TDD.
notes:
Primary files: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/query_service.rs, apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/query_service.rs.
Primary TDD IDs: PW-CON-001..006, PW-SES-012, RS-QS-001..012.
close_reason: Fixed: QueryService now pages/filter in SQL, resolves sibling runtime paths, and replays archived PTY history as per-seq frames with explicit gap availability

Extend `crates/daemon/src/ipc/handshake.rs` and `crates/daemon/src/ipc/descriptor.rs` without replacing the Layer 1 wire shape. The ground truth already exists in `handshake.rs`: `ClientMessage::Hello` is still the first client frame; `ServerMessage::Welcome` still carries the welcome field names; raw pre-router mutation traffic still rejects as `mutations_unavailable` until the command router is active.

- **Quality gate commands:**
  - `cargo test -p daemon --test ipc_handshake`

- `crates/daemon/src/ipc/descriptor.rs` — Align descriptor/bootstrap behavior with repeated authenticated connections

## Spec Requirements (from §1.5)

**L2-FR-DB.2 — Handshake Negotiates Compatibility and Restart Semantics**
- AC1: The first daemon-wire message remains `hello`, and the daemon responds with `welcome`.
- AC2: Welcome fields stay aligned with the current daemon truth: protocol version, daemon version, `instanceId`, `schemaEpoch`, `commitSeq`, health, mutation allowance, active sessions, reconnect outcome, and stream-resume permission.
- AC3: `lastSeenInstanceId` mismatch remains the restart-invalidated trigger.

**L2-FR-DB.15 — Layer 2 Extends the Handshake-Only IPC Envelope**
- AC1: The Layer 1 handshake stays additive.
- AC2: The socket becomes reusable for later `command` / `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` traffic after successful handshake.
- AC3: Pre-router mutation traffic is still rejected on the handshake-only path.

## Tests to Pass

No unique Layer 2 TDD IDs are homed here. This additive-handshake bead must still satisfy:

- `cargo check --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The additive `hello`/`welcome` exchange remains intact.
2. Reconnect outcome and restart invalidation behavior remain aligned with the current daemon wire contract.
3. The bead does not prematurely claim desktop-side bridge tests before the bridge exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
Verbatim spec anchors:

**L3-FR-4.1.1 — `validation_verdicts` stores full local-only validator reasoning**
- AC1: `validation_verdicts` links worker and validator jobs/sessions and stores verdict identity, confidence, summary, `basis_sufficiency`, incident signature, `enforcement_eligible`, issue JSON, and run-manifest hash.
- AC2: Operator override fields (`override_verdict`, `override_reason`, `override_by`, `override_at`) exist from first activation.
- AC3: The table is local-only; Layer 4 later derives redacted `validation_verdict_summaries` from it without requiring a duplicate local summary table in Layer 3.

**L3-FR-4.1.2 — `source_runtime_state` persists breaker/health state per source**
- AC1: `source_runtime_state` is keyed by `source_id` and records health color, circuit state, challenge counters/window, cooldown timestamps, latest canary outcome, and last error code.
- AC2: The table is the local operational authority for source-health and circuit-breaker transitions.
- AC3: Persisted fields are sufficient to audit why a source is `closed`, `half_open`, or `open`.

**L3-FR-4.1.3 — `listing_evidence` activates as a trust-aware local cache**
- AC1: `listing_evidence` stores source identity, listing identity, normalized title, structured attributes, parsed standards/units, seller/commercial fields, freshness timestamps, and detail-fetch flags.
- AC2: The table carries `trust_state` with default `unverified` plus `source_job_id` for provenance/trust tracing.
- AC3: Uniqueness is enforced on `(source, source_listing_id)`, and source-specific freshness TTLs match the table in this section.

**L3-FR-4.1.4 — `process_relations` stores push-owned relation edges**
- AC1: `process_relations` stores both process IDs, `relation_type`, `confidence_bps`, supporting evidence, and the standard sync-tracking fields.
- AC2: Stored `relation_type` values remain constrained to evidence-bearing non-`separate` outcomes: `merged_same_process`, `related_not_merged`, and `possible_duplicate`; `separate` stays an evaluated outcome but writes no row.
- AC3: The table is push-owned so relation state can become shared visibility in Layer 4 without changing authority.

**L3-FR-4.1.5 — `process_aliases` stores push-owned redirects for retired process IDs**
- AC1: `process_aliases` maps `alias_process_id` to `canonical_process_id` with an `alias_reason` and the full standard push-owned sync columns including `stage_run_id`.
- AC2: Alias rows preserve deep-link stability after relation-driven merges.
- AC3: The alias table is push-owned and remains separate from the full cluster model carried by `canonical_process_id`.

### 4.2 Modified Tables

| Table | Field | Change in L3 |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| `workflow_jobs` | `parent_job_id` | Now actively used — links validator sub-jobs to worker jobs |
| `workflow_jobs` | `validation_required` | Now actively set by Validation Policy Engine (still defaults false) |
| `workflow_jobs` | `validation_verdict_id` | Now populated after validation completes |
| `agent_session_logs` | `run_manifest_path` | Now actively populated by Run Manifest Writer |
| `agent_session_logs` | `run_manifest_hash` | Now actively populated (SHA-256 of manifest) |

**L3-FR-4.2.1 — Layer 3 activates its forward-compatible columns on existing tables**
- AC1: `workflow_jobs.parent_job_id` links validator sub-jobs to worker jobs in live Layer 3 behavior.
- AC2: `workflow_jobs.validation_required` and `workflow_jobs.validation_verdict_id` are actively populated by validation policy/execution.
- AC3: `agent_session_logs.run_manifest_path` and `agent_session_logs.run_manifest_hash` are populated for every manifest-producing session.

### 4.3 Authority Classification (L3 Additions)

| Table | Authority | Rationale |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| `validation_verdicts` | Local-only | Full verdict reasoning too large/sensitive for sync |
| `source_runtime_state` | Local-only | Per-daemon operational state |
| `listing_evidence` | Local-only | Cache layer, not authoritative data |
| `process_relations` | Push-owned | Shared visibility in Layer 4 |
| `process_aliases` | Push-owned | Stable deep links across desktop/web |

**L3-FR-4.3.1 — Layer 3 table authority classes are fixed at activation**
- AC1: `validation_verdicts`, `source_runtime_state`, and `listing_evidence` are local-only.
- AC2: `process_relations` and `process_aliases` are push-owned.
- AC3: No Layer 3 table introduced in this section mixes local and remote authority.

### 4.4 Four-Layer Observability Model

| Layer | Content | Storage | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|---------|
| **Control events** | Job lifecycle, stage transitions, decision points, resource grants/denials, circuit breaker state changes | Structured JSON logs (tracing crate) | Operational monitoring, alerting |
| **Protocol events** | Agent communication, skill loading, checkpoint progression, result contract events, adapter events | Structured JSON in `agent_session_logs.structured_trace` | Debugging, replay, performance |
| **Forensic bytes** | Raw PTY output OR contract-mode stdout/stderr | Compressed immutable artifacts at `terminal_output_path` | Post-incident analysis, deterministic replay |
| **Narrative** | Run manifests — agent-written narrative + daemon evidence appendix | Immutable artifacts at `run_manifest_path` | Semantic validation, operator review |

All four layers capture data from both PTY and contract-mode sessions.

**Correlation and retention rules:**
- Every layer is keyed by `job_id`; session-scoped artifacts additionally carry `session_id`; process-facing surfaces carry `process_id`; validator records carry both worker and validator job/session identities plus `run_manifest_hash`.
- The minimum audit trail for a 3 AM failure is verdict -> `validation_verdicts.worker_session_id` / `run_manifest_hash` -> `agent_session_logs.run_manifest_path` -> appendix `artifact_refs` / `terminal_output_path` -> structured control/protocol traces.
- Minimum L3 retention: control/protocol traces `30` days, raw forensic bytes `14` days or until linked error manifests are resolved (whichever is longer), and run manifests plus `validation_verdicts` `180` days and never shorter than the lifetime of linked workflow/error/backlog records.

Required verification IDs:
- `CI-L3-001`
- `CI-L3-005`
- `L3-T-schema_activation-001`
- `L3-T-schema_activation-002`
- `L3-T-schema_activation-003`
- `L3-T-schema_activation-004`
- `L3-T-schema_activation-005`
- `L3-T-schema_activation-006`

Representative exact TDD assertions:
- `CI-L3-001`: `cargo check --all-targets` exits `0` for the daemon workspace after Layer 3 modules, migrations, and tests are added
- `CI-L3-005`: module inventory matches the 12 new Layer 3 daemon surfaces, `migrations/0005_l3_operational_hardening.sql` exists, the 18 predeclared test files exist, additive files are present, and the Layer 3 skill filesystem inventory matches the spec
- `L3-T-schema_activation-001`: applying the Layer 3 migration creates `validation_verdicts`, `source_runtime_state`, `listing_evidence`, `process_relations`, and `process_aliases` with the declared columns and key constraints
- `L3-T-schema_activation-002`: `source_runtime_state` includes `circuit_state` and `last_canary_result` at migration time; runtime does not rely on opportunistic `ALTER TABLE` drift to discover L3 shape
- `L3-T-schema_activation-005`: `process_relations` stores only `merged_same_process`, `related_not_merged`, and `possible_duplicate`; `separate` remains a computed outcome that writes no relation row

acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
Verbatim spec anchors:

**L3-FR-1.3.1 — `scheduler/cron.rs` owns daemon-local cron scheduling**
- AC1: Layer 3 includes `scheduler/cron.rs`.
- AC2: The module schedules and enqueues agent work from cron definitions inside the daemon rather than via external schedulers.
- AC3: The module preserves explicit skill binding and startup catchup behavior as defined in §1.5.

**L3-FR-1.3.2 — `sources/registry.rs` owns typed source definitions and mutable runtime binding**
- AC1: Layer 3 includes `sources/registry.rs`.
- AC2: The module stores typed source definitions with version tracking, skill binding, schedules, and health/cooldown status.
- AC3: Static source definitions remain rooted in `sources`, while mutable runtime state is read from and written to `source_runtime_state`.

**L3-FR-1.5.1 — Cron scheduling freezes the executable skill binding at enqueue time**
- AC1: Every cron-enqueued job stores `source_id`, `skill_id`, `skill_version`, `cron_expression`, and enablement/next-run state as part of its scheduling definition.
- AC2: The scheduler freezes `skill_id + skill_version` when the job is enqueued and does not resolve a newer skill version later at execution time.
- AC3: If the scheduler cannot admit a due job immediately, the bound job remains queued/runnable with its original frozen binding.
- AC4: Cron roots enqueue through the ordinary `EnqueueJobRequest` surface, leaving `parent_job_id = NULL` for root jobs and preserving the same job-claim/visibility-fence semantics as manually triggered work.

**L3-FR-1.5.2 — Catchup sweeps and source suppression are explicit scheduler behaviors**
- AC1: On daemon start after downtime, the scheduler detects overdue runs and processes them in priority order rather than flooding the system.
- AC2: Catchup execution still passes through the Resource Arbiter and therefore respects typed quotas during recovery.
- AC3: If a source circuit is open or cooling down, normal ingestion for that source is suppressed and only `source-health/*` or `auth-refresh/*` jobs may be scheduled.

### 1.6 PTY Hardening

| Hardening | What It Does | Why It Matters |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| **fd hygiene** | Aggressively close inherited fds before exec | macOS Big Sur/Cocoa and GNOME/Mutter can leak fds into child processes, causing intermittent failures |
| **EIO handling** | Treat EIO on PTY master read (after slave closes) as normal termination | Without this, EIO after slave close looks like an internal error |
| **Terminal geometry** | Fix PTY size for headless runs (e.g., 120x40) | CLI formatting and browser/tool behavior must be stable. Only resize when operator attaches for live viewing |
| **Signal handling** | Use signals only as wakeups, then drain waitpid/wait loops until nothing left to reap | Signals may be coalesced by Tokio's Unix signal streams |

**L3-FR-3.4.1 — Source-health canaries execute a fixed six-check health contract**
- AC1: Each canary checks reachability, page fingerprint, auth state where applicable, geo/locale correctness, challenge rate, and minimal extraction.
- AC2: Each failed check maps to an explicit failure classification: `SOURCE_UNREACHABLE`, `SOURCE_LAYOUT_CHANGED`, `AGENT_AUTH_CHALLENGE`, `SOURCE_LOCALE_DRIFT`, `SOURCE_BLOCKED`, or `SOURCE_EXTRACTION_FAILED`.
- AC3: The canary surface is lightweight enough to run ahead of scheduled production work rather than as a substitute for full ingestion.
- AC4: The named failure classifications in this section are logical source-health classes; they map onto the existing 28-variant `ErrorCode` surface plus structured context rather than introducing hidden enum additions.

**L3-FR-3.4.2 — Source-health runs on a higher-frequency cadence and suppresses unhealthy production work**
- AC1: Active-source canaries run every `30` minutes by default.
- AC2: If the most recent canary failed or timed out, production ingestion/enrichment jobs for that source are suppressed until health recovers.
- AC3: Canary success, failure, and timeout outcomes are all persisted as explicit source-runtime signals rather than inferred later from missing work.

### 3.5 Source Circuit Breaker

Repeated challenge-class failures trigger a circuit breaker that protects the source account/IP.

**Three states:**

```text
CLOSED (healthy)
  → repeated failures → HALF_OPEN (canary-only)
  → canary fails → OPEN (paused)
  → canary succeeds → CLOSED

HALF_OPEN
  → canary succeeds → CLOSED
  → canary fails → OPEN

OPEN
  → cooldown expires → HALF_OPEN
  → manual reset → HALF_OPEN
```

| State | Allowed Jobs | Duration |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `closed` | All jobs for this source | Normal operation |
| `half_open` | Only `source-health/*` and `auth-refresh/*` canary/auth jobs | Until canary succeeds |
| `open` | No jobs for this source | Configurable cooldown (default 2 hours), then auto-transitions to `half_open` |

**Trigger criteria:** Circuit opens after N consecutive challenge-class failures (default N=3) within a time window. Challenge-class failures include `AGENT_AUTH_CHALLENGE`, `SOURCE_CAPTCHA_BLOCKED`, and `SOURCE_SOFT_BLOCKED` when structured context classifies the blocker as `source_blocked` or `source_rate_limited`.

**State persisted in:** `source_runtime_state` table (local-only — see §4 for DDL).

**L3-FR-3.5.1 — `closed` source circuits permit normal scheduling**
- AC1: In `closed`, all jobs for the source remain eligible for normal scheduling.
- AC2: `closed` represents healthy operation until challenge-class failures accumulate past the configured threshold.
- AC3: Transition out of `closed` is driven by the explicit breaker rules in this section rather than ad hoc operator judgment.

**L3-FR-3.5.2 — `half_open` source circuits are canary-only recovery mode**
- AC1: In `half_open`, only `source-health/*` and `auth-refresh/*` jobs are allowed for that source.
- AC2: A successful canary from `half_open` transitions the source back to `closed`.
- AC3: A failed or timed-out canary from `half_open` transitions the source to `open`.

**L3-FR-3.5.3 — `open` source circuits pause normal work until cooldown expiry or manual reset**
- AC1: In `open`, no normal jobs for the source are admitted.
- AC2: `open` lasts for a configurable cooldown with default duration `2 hours`.
- AC3: Cooldown expiry or manual reset transitions the source to `half_open`, not directly to `closed`.

**L3-FR-3.5.4 — Breaker trigger criteria and state persistence are explicit**
- AC1: The circuit opens after `N=3` consecutive challenge-class failures within the configured time window unless configuration overrides the default.
- AC2: Challenge-class failures include `AGENT_AUTH_CHALLENGE`, `SOURCE_CAPTCHA_BLOCKED`, and `SOURCE_SOFT_BLOCKED` with structured blocker class `source_blocked` or `source_rate_limited`.
- AC3: `source_runtime_state` persists the last health state, circuit state, challenge-window counters, cooldown timestamps, latest canary outcome, and last error code so state transitions are auditable.
- AC4: Circuit transitions execute transactionally per `source_id`; newer canary timestamps win over stale writes, and a stale success may not silently close a more recent `open`/`half_open` state.

### 3.6 Relation Resolution Engine

**Module:** `packages/intelligence/src/relations/resolve-process-relations.ts`

**Purpose:** Classify notice-to-process relations after normalization. Runs as stage 3 of the pipeline.

**Four classifications:**

| Classification | Meaning | Action |
|---------------|---------|--------|
| `merged_same_process` | Same OCID or explicit linked notice chain | Merge into single `ProcurementProcess`; retired ID gets `process_aliases` redirect |
| `related_not_merged` | Framework/call-off, planning/tender, same buyer + subject but different OCIDs | Create `ProcessRelation` edge for cache sharing; keep separate processes |
| `possible_duplicate` | High-similarity pair but not confident enough for auto-merge | Hold for operator review; create `ProcessRelation` edge |
| `separate` | No meaningful relationship | No action |

**Resolution algorithm:**

1. **Hard blockers check** — contradictions that prevent merging regardless of similarity:
   - Conflicting exact reference numbers
   - Framework establishment vs call-off/award mismatch
   - Explicit different OCIDs with separate-process semantics (e.g., direct award after unsuccessful competition)
   - Incompatible stage chronology
   - Same buyer but clearly different lot/value/reference structure

2. **Exact-match rules** — deterministic classification:
   - Same OCID → `merged_same_process`
   - Explicit related-notice reference with plausible stage sequence → `merged_same_process`
   - Framework/call-off relation detected → `related_not_merged`

3. **Heuristic scoring** (non-blocked, non-exact pairs only):

   The MVP weight vector is deterministic and versioned as `relation_model_version = 1`. The evaluated feature vector, blockers hit, model version, and threshold bucket are persisted in `process_relations.evidence` (or merge-audit metadata) so the same input pair yields the same replayable decision.

   ```
   merge_score =
     0.35 * reference_match
   + 0.20 * buyer_match
   + 0.20 * title_similarity
   + 0.10 * cpv_overlap
   + 0.10 * date_proximity
   + 0.05 * value_proximity
   ```

   - >= 0.95 with no blocker → `merged_same_process`
   - 0.75–0.94 → `related_not_merged` or `possible_duplicate` (for operator review)
   - < 0.75 → `separate`

4. **Edge creation** — `related_not_merged` and `possible_duplicate` pairs always get a `ProcessRelation` edge enabling cache sharing of search results and listing evidence across the cluster. `merged_same_process` may persist an audit edge, but `separate` writes no `process_relations` row.

5. **Alias management** — when a previously published process ID is retired by a merge, write a `process_aliases` redirect so desktop/web deep links remain stable.

6. **Cluster identity assignment** — every `ProcurementProcess` carries a `canonical_process_id` (defaults to self). On merge, resolve both inputs to their current canonical roots first, then choose the surviving root deterministically (`earliest created_at`, UUID tie-breaker). The retired process's `canonical_process_id` points to the root. Rollups, manifests, and deep links resolve through `canonical_process_id`, not raw `process_id`. The `process_aliases` table handles redirects, but `canonical_process_id` is the full merge model.

7. **Late merge as decision-staleness event** — if two already-enriched processes merge after operator review:
   - All relevant `pending_operator_intents` / `operator_decision_heads` entries are marked stale (`decision_stale = true`)
   - Manifest is regenerated for the merged cluster
   - `pipeline_assessments` recomputed at cluster level
   - Operator sees explicit "identity changed after review" notification
   - This prevents technically correct sync with semantically wrong decisions

   If no operator decision or pending intent exists yet, the engine still regenerates the cluster rollup/manifest but does **not** emit a spurious stale-decision incident.

**New tables:** `process_relations` (push-owned) and `process_aliases` (push-owned). See §4 for full DDL.

**Conservative thresholds:** Default thresholds are deliberately conservative. False merges are harder to undo than false separations. The operator can manually merge `possible_duplicate` pairs.

**Weight variation by context:** The global weights above are a bootstrap default. Weights should eventually vary by source-pair and notice-stage-pair:
- Planning → tender → award: values drift significantly across lifecycle stages
- Call-offs share buyer/CPV/title but may differ on reference semantics
- FTS vs Contracts Finder duplicates may normalise references differently

For MVP, the global weights are acceptable. A simple interpretable logistic model per source-pair / stage-pair fitted from adjudicated pairs can replace them later — keep the rule engine and hard blockers, fit only the soft weights.

**Additional features for future improvement:** Normalised buyer registration/authority identifier, contact email/domain similarity, lot-count similarity, postcode/region, procurement method / notice type compatibility, reference edit distance after stripping amendment/lot suffixes, document hash overlap if available.

**UI grouping before perfect merge:** To reduce false non-merge cost without destructive auto-merge, group `related_not_merged` and `possible_duplicate` in the desktop UI as a cluster card with relation confidence. Share caches cautiously within the cluster. Let the operator see one cluster view with constituent processes.

## Acceptance Criteria
Verbatim spec anchors:

**L3-FR-1.3.5 — `pty/hardening.rs` owns PTY-specific reliability protections**
- AC1: Layer 3 includes `pty/hardening.rs`.
- AC2: The module implements fd hygiene, PTY `EIO` handling, fixed geometry for headless runs, and signal-as-wakeup wait draining.
- AC3: PTY hardening changes terminal/runtime reliability only and does not redefine business pipeline semantics.

**L3-FR-1.6.1 — PTY sessions apply the full hardening bundle before being treated as reliable**
- AC1: Child exec paths aggressively close inherited fds before exec so unrelated parent fds are not leaked into browser/CLI descendants.
- AC2: `EIO` on PTY master read after slave closure is treated as expected hangup, while unexpected active-session PTY read failure still follows an explicit cleanup/error path.
- AC3: Headless PTY runs default to a stable fixed geometry of `120x40` and only resize on explicit operator attachment.
- AC4: Unix signals act as wakeups only; the daemon drains `waitpid`/wait loops until no more children remain to reap.
- AC5: PTY hardening preserves the existing session lifecycle ordering `Created -> Spawned -> Active -> Terminating -> Exited -> Reaped -> Archived` rather than inventing a separate hardening-specific state machine.
- AC6: Expected post-slave-close hangup does not require a dedicated new `PtySessionError` variant; unexpected PTY I/O still flows through the existing `PtySessionError` classification surface with explicit context.

### 1.7 Host Environment Awareness

- **Sleep/wake:** If host suspends during active session, assume browser-driven PTY sessions are tainted. Use monotonic time for stall detection. Emit `HOST_SLEEP_INTERRUPTED` if suspend gap exceeds configurable threshold.
- **Missed runs:** On daemon start after extended downtime, catchup sweep checks for overdue jobs. Jobs executed in priority order via resource arbiter.
